prompt:
Write an original wilderness adventure story titled "The Second Cairn".

Write the story in English.
Use third-person narration outside quoted speech and dreams.
Narrate unfolding actions in the past tense; timeless mechanism explanations may use the present tense.
Preserve this mechanism rule: The river gate moves only when its hand capstan is turned; the intact gate has no motor, remote control or automatic release.
Follow the supplied three-chapter event order.
Keep the route book intact until its custody transfer in chapter three; temporary inspection or handling is allowed.
Keep Jun alive through the end of chapter three.
Treat remembered scenes, dreams, plans and hypotheses according to their stated temporal or epistemic status.

Use the supplied Bible and outline. Maintain natural prose and the difference between a suspicion and an established fact.

outline.title: Two Marks in the Rain
outline.purpose: Develop the designed events through action and dialogue.
outline.turn: The expedition register named Jun as the apprentice navigator.
hookSeeds: Beyond the marked turn stood a second cairn with a flat black stone, absent from the current route sheet.
A red thread crossed the old route-book stitch, and no entry explained who had repaired it.
A two-note whistle sounded from upriver after dark, with no visible boat to answer it.

outline.title: Above the Flood Line
outline.purpose: Develop the designed events through action and dialogue.
outline.turn: Rafi appointed Jun acting route leader for the exposed traverse.
hookSeeds: Jun found an old cut arrow beneath the second cairn’s black stone, pointing towards the high traverse.
A numbered depot stamp crossed the red thread, connecting the repair to an old inventory but naming no repairer.
The same unexplained two-note whistle sounded beyond the flooded bend while they secured the canoe.

outline.title: A Place to Put the Book
outline.purpose: Develop the designed events through action and dialogue.
outline.turn: The expedition office appointed Jun expedition navigator over the radio.
hookSeeds: An old route sheet at the landing confirmed that the second cairn marked the entrance to the high traverse.
The red-thread repairer was still unnamed when Jun put the route book away.
The relief crew recognised the whistle’s two notes as an old ferry signal, but could not explain who was sounding it now.

authorIntent: Let practical cooperation and changing evidence alter trust without treating unknowns as confirmed facts.
currentFocus: Preserve quantities, custody, epistemic qualifications and the difference between past and current events.
